title: EON Stream revocation list (v0 — UNSTABLE)
description: A signed statement of which module versions and which signing keys must no longer be trusted. Revocation is listed before signing in docs/signing-and-revocation.md for a reason: signing without revocation only proves who shipped the malicious version, it does not stop it. v0 is explicitly unstable.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS schema the document is written against.

issuedAt.description: When this list was issued. Also acts as its version: a client refuses a list whose issuedAt is not strictly newer than the one it holds, because replaying yesterday's list is the same attack as blocking today's.

nextUpdate.description: When a client should have a newer list. Past this the list is stale and the client says so — but it keeps applying it. Falling back to 'nothing is revoked' would mean an attacker who can block a network request can un-revoke.

revoked.description: Revoked module versions. Version-scoped, not module-scoped: a single bad release should not destroy a maintainer's project.

id.description: Identifier of the revoked module, as in its manifest.

versions.description: Which versions, in npm range syntax. A bare version pins exactly that one. Note the edge semantics: '<1.5.0' covers pre-releases below 1.5.0, while '>=1.0.0 <1.5.0' excludes 1.0.0-alpha because semver orders it below 1.0.0 — so 'everything before the fix' is written as the upper bound alone.

reason.description: Enumerated, not free text, so a client can treat malicious-code differently from publisher-request — and so this list cannot become a channel for arbitrary prose shown to users.

advisory.description: Where a person can read the detail. A revoked module is disabled and reported with this link, never quietly removed: quiet removal teaches users to distrust the updater.

revokedKeys.description: Revoked signing keys. Revoking a key revokes everything it signed, unless a newer valid signature exists.

signature.description: Detached signature over this document with the signature member removed — the only thing 'detached' can mean for a document carrying its own signature. The subject is { id: 'org.eon.stream.revocation', version: <issuedAt>, sha256: <hash of the unsigned document> }, which is what makes one list's signature non-transferable to another. Signed with the release key, so a revocation can be published without reaching for the module key.
